  Terse gloss: "Nergal-Sharezer; a Babylonian official present at the fall of Jerusalem, bearing a name meaning 'Nergal, protect the king.'"
  Readable gloss: "A compound Akkadian proper name borne by a Babylonian official in Nebuchadnezzar's entourage during the siege and fall of Jerusalem in 586 BCE. The name combines the Babylonian deity Nergal with the prayer element 'protect the king' (shar-usur). He appears in Jeremiah 39:3,13, where he is listed among the officials who entered Jerusalem after its walls were breached, and who later facilitated the release of Jeremiah from prison at Nebuchadnezzar's command."

  Sense 1: "Nergal-Saretser (Babylonian official)"

In Jeremiah 39:3 he is named among those who sat in the middle gate of Jerusalem after its fall, and in Jer 39:13 he participates in the delegation that retrieves Jeremiah...
    Existing Spanish translations: Etser, Nergal, oficial-de, y-Nergal-Sar-Etser
